aggregation_order: Choose an admissible deterministic algorithm using public N, m, and n, then take the supremum of its full output gap over all admissible matrices.
source_fields.complete_expression: r_{\rm det}^{\star}(N;m,n)=\inf_{\mathcal A\in\mathfrak A_{\rm det}:\,\sup_A N_{\rm matvec}(\mathcal A,A)\le N}\sup_{A\in[-1,1]^{m\times n}}\left[\max_{v\in\Delta_m}v^{\mathsf T}A\widehat x-\min_{u\in\Delta_n}\widehat y^{\mathsf T}Au\right]
source_fields.quantifier_order: choose a single algorithm from public inputs, then all compatible hidden instances and legal oracle rules
source_fields.time_uniformity: Optimal worst-case output error at fixed input budget $N$. No simultaneous guarantee over all stopping times is asserted.

description_paragraphs: The loss is $\operatorname{Gap}(\widehat x,\widehat y)=\max_{v\in\Delta_m}v^{\mathsf T}A\widehat x-\min_{u\in\Delta_n}\widehat y^{\mathsf T}Au$. It lies in $[0,2]$.

description_paragraphs: The hidden matrix is $A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}$, with $\max_{i,j}|A_{ij}|\le1$ and public positive integers $m,n$.
$\Delta_k=\{u\in\mathbb R^k:u\ge0,\ \mathbf1^{\mathsf T}u=1\}$ for every positive integer $k$. Both strategy sets are compact and convex, and a saddle point exists.

assumptions.description: The hidden matrix is $A\in[-1,1]^{m\times n}$; every entry lies in $[-1,1]$.
assumptions.scope: All point pairs in the declared function domain. Blockwise constants are uniform in the remaining fixed variables.

model.parameter_domain_description: $N$: positive integer; $m$: integer at least 2; $n$: integer at least 2. Derived quantities are defined in the parameter table. Each region states any additional accuracy and dimension conditions.

description_paragraphs: For arbitrary vectors $(x,y)\in\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R^m$, one query returns the exact bundle $(Ax,A^{\mathsf T}y)$. Query vectors need not be probability vectors.

One bundled left/right multiplication costs one call. A single-direction multiplication is obtained by setting the other query vector to zero. The matrix is fixed before interaction and its entries are not directly accessible.
Dimensions and strategy sets are public. The requested budget or accuracy is specified by the comparison quantity for the selected view.

operations.coupling: Deterministic exact responses with repeated queries allowed; stochastic sample-reuse permissions are irrelevant.

operations.order_convention: This operation is charged according to its explicit input and output, not renamed according to a scalar function's derivative order.

public_inputs: Public inputs include matrix dimensions $m,n$ and budget $N$, together with the declared initial point and feasible-set information. No analytic representation of the hidden function, operator, or matrix is disclosed.
oracle.query_domain_description: Queries may use any $(x,y)\in\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R^m$; the query vectors need not lie in the strategy simplices.

description_paragraphs: Return $(\widehat x,\widehat y)\in\Delta_n\times\Delta_m$. Unqueried outputs and arbitrary measurable transcript postprocessing are permitted; no certificate is required.

description_paragraphs: One bundled two-sided query increments $N_{\rm matvec}$ by one. A single right or transpose product can be obtained by setting the other input to zero and is charged as one bundled call.
Use a fixed worst-case budget: calls never exceed the prespecified $N$ on any instance or random execution path. Earlier stopping within the budget is permitted.
